ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and officers against the Gibraltar Sanctions List, HM Treasury Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and EU restrictive measures as transposed under Gibraltar law. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates; ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening are mandatory under GFSC AML/CFT Rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry e-Services Portal (Companies House Gibraltar online filing system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in English or in Latin-script transliteration. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the transliteration must be phonetically and visually distinct from any existing registered name. Names must comply with the Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), avoiding names that are misleading, offensive, or identical or too similar to an existing company on the register. In the case of a Bermuda Exempted Company, a Gibraltar subsidiary may use a parent-suffix convention or require consent wording if 'Bermuda' appears in the name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days, accompanied by a written statement of grounds and supporting evidence. The Registrar must issue a reasoned decision within 21 days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. A fresh name application may be filed immediately, provided the proposed name is materially distinct from the rejected name and does not conflict with other registered names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible. Gibraltar law requires a physical registered office in Gibraltar (s. 92, Companies Act 2014, as amended). A licensed corporate service provider's physical address may be used; however, a purely virtual or mail-forwarding address does not satisfy the statutory requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of unannounced on-site physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation, reflecting GFSC's enhanced economic substance and registered office inspection protocols applied to digital and EdTech businesses that do not maintain a visible physical footprint in Gibraltar.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 5–10 (Incorporation), s. 33 (Memorandum and Articles), s. 57 (Registered Office), ss. 101–105 (Directors and Secretary); combined with the Income Tax (Qualifying Companies) Regulations 2011 for tax-exempt status, mirroring the Bermuda Exempted Company template; Data Protection Act 2019 (Gibraltar) for EdTech data processing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar, 5 Secretary's Lane, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form G (Application for Registration of a Company) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form N (Statutory Declaration of Compliance).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a private company limited by shares may adopt a nominal capital of GIP 1.00 or any stated currency; subscriber shares may be issued at par with no escrow deposit requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the allotment of subscribers' ordinary shares set out in the register of members is hereby ratified and accepted in full; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be established and continuously maintained at the office of the licensed corporate service provider in Gibraltar; (3) [Name] is appointed Director and [Name] is appointed Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until removed by ordinary resolution; (4) the officers are authorized to file the statutory declaration, open bank and EMI accounts, and execute Gibraltar Income Tax registration; (5) the common seal, if adopted, shall be affixed only by the Director and Secretary acting jointly. THIS RESOLUTION was duly passed on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Clearance and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (e-Registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed names in order of preference via the licensed corporate service provider. Verify that the name does not contain restricted words (e.g. 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance') absent a separate licence, and that it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Obtain written name approval or a formal reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (three alternatives)
Cover letter from licensed corporate service provider
Certificate of Good Standing of subscriber (if corporate subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on similarity grounds, file Form 2 (Objection) within 14 days or promptly select the next priority name; no filing fee is forfeited for a substitute name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Corporate Service Provider and Notary Public (Gibraltar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with Companies Act 2014 model articles, including authorised share capital, objects clause (software development and interactive education), and adoption of the exempt company tax status election. Arrange execution by each subscriber before a notary public or authorised witness, and prepare Form N (Statutory Declaration of Compliance).
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft in English)
Form N - Statutory Declaration of Compliance
Passport or national ID of each subscriber
Proof of registered office address consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any clause (e.g. objects or share structure), amend the M&A via a supplementary board resolution and resubmit the clean copy within 14 days of the query notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form G and Payment of Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form G electronically or in person at the Registry, accompanied by two signed copies of the M&A, Form N, and the registered office consent. Pay the statutory incorporation fee (approx. GIP 90) via bank transfer or card. Request same-day service if expedited incorporation is required.
required_dossiers: Form G (Application for Registration)
Two signed copies of Memorandum and Articles
Form N (Declaration of Compliance)
Registered office address consent letter
Copy of board resolution authorising the filing (if corporate subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incompleteness, the Registry issues a non-compliance notice; applicant has 14 days to supply corrective documentation, failing which the application lapses and the fee is refunded less a minimal admin charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation evidencing the company's legal existence and file number. Obtain certified copies of the certificate and the stamped M&A for use in bank account opening and tax registrations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form G receipt of filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, submit Form 3 (Correction of Particulars) with a covering affidavit; the Registrar will reissue a corrected certificate within 5 business days, or apply to the Supreme Court for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office (Gibraltar), Financial Services Commission (GFSC), and Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office within 21 days of incorporation; file the Register of Beneficial Owners with the GFSC under the Beneficial Ownership (Access) Regulations; and, because the business is EdTech, register as a data controller with the GRA under the Data Protection Act 2019. Obtain a tax exempt company / qualifying company certificate if electing exempt status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Form 1 (Income Tax registration) for Gibraltar
Register of Directors, Secretary, and Beneficial Owners
Board minutes appointing officers
Identity and address verification of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration of the beneficial ownership return incurs a fixed penalty; file a voluntary corrective return within 30 days and submit a written mitigation statement to the GFSC to reduce or waive penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial plant; for any physical office premises, the Town Planning and Building Control Department, HM Government of Gibraltar, issues an Occupancy Certificate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (software/SaaS activity is unlicensed in Gibraltar). Mandatory non-industrial registrations: (i) Data Controller Registration under the Data Protection Act 2019 with the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority; (ii) Qualifying Company tax-exemption certificate from the Income Tax Office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category D) - office and cloud-based digital services produce no physical works; no EIA screening or environmental permit required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for serverless EdTech operations; if an office is leased, general municipal waste handling must comply with the Environmental Protection Regulations (Gibraltar) and any e-waste must be surrendered to a WEEE-compliant collector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the leased Gibraltar office: obtain a Fire Safety Certificate and annual fire risk assessment under the Fire Safety Act (Gibraltar) from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; secure structural and electrical inspection approval via the Building Control Department; register the workplace under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar) and appoint a Health and Safety Officer if more than five employees; obtain an Occupancy Certificate before staff take residence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation); UK VAT authority where applicable: HM Revenue & Customs, VAT Registration Service (https://www.gov.uk/vat-registration)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company (BM_EXEMPTED_CO) receives no automatic Gibraltar tax ID. If it has no Gibraltar establishment or Gibraltar-source income, no Gibraltar tax registration is required. If a Gibraltar nexus arises, the entity must register as a foreign/overseas company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry, then apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a tax reference by submitting the Bermuda certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office certificate, director/shareholder registers, and evidence of substance. For direct UK B2C digital sales, register with HMRC as a non-established taxable person through the Non-Union VAT Mini One-Stop Shop (VATOSS) or standard VAT registration; HMRC issues a GB VAT number and may require platform transaction records and payment evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Gibraltar or Bermuda for entity classification. Bermuda exempted status is irrevocably elected by incorporation under the Bermuda Companies Act 1981 and maintained with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies. For indirect taxes, the entity may elect UK Non-Union VATOSS registration for B2C digital services, or rely on Apple IAP/Google Play Billing as merchant-of-record arrangements. No hybrid mismatch or offshore exempt-company election is available under Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010; tax treatment is determined by actual residence and economic substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar: no VAT/GST/sales or use tax. UK VAT (20%) is destination-based and may apply to B2C digital education supplies to UK consumers when the Bermuda/Gibraltar entity is the supplier; Apple IAP and Google Play Billing normally act as merchant-of-record and collect applicable UK VAT on platform sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar: nil threshold because no VAT registration exists. UK VAT: no turnover threshold for a non-established supplier making B2C supplies of digital services to UK consumers; the UK GBP 90,000 threshold applicable to UK-established businesses does not govern a foreign entity supplying digital services to UK consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar has no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no mandatory e-invoicing/API clearance regime. UK VAT compliance is electronic under HMRC Making Tax Digital (MTD) when registration applies, with VAT returns filed via MTD-compatible software or the VATOSS portal; there is no government invoice stamping or real-time transaction clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar zero-rating is not applicable because Gibraltar imposes no VAT. Under UK VAT, digital language-learning software supplied to overseas business customers is outside the scope of UK VAT when the recipient belongs outside the UK and reverse-charge or local tax rules apply; B2C supplies to non-UK consumers are not subject to UK VAT because the place of supply is the consumer's country. UK export zero-rating is limited to qualifying physical exported goods, not pure digital subscriptions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable: pure EdTech subscription services are delivered digitally, with no physical export of goods from Gibraltar or the UK.

If physical course materials were exported, the required bundle would be the Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading or air waybill, commercial invoice, proof of payment, and bank inward-remittance evidence.
No customs or Bill of Lading evidence is required for SaaS or online tutoring under Gibraltar or UK VAT rules.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar has no VAT clawback mechanism because no VAT is assessed. UK VAT inaccuracies, fraudulent zero-rating, or inappropriate treatment of UK digital B2C supplies as outside scope expose the entity to HMRC assessments, interest, and penalty exposure up to 100% under VATA 1994 and FA 2007 Schedule 24. Refund or zero-rating claims without customer contracts, payment evidence, IP logs, and platform merchant records will be rejected and clawed back. The 180-day period is treated as the internal compliance ceiling for repatriating export revenue; neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda imposes a statutory FX repatriation deadline, but a Bermuda exempted company must keep its exempted status by avoiding domestic Bermuda business activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the prudential and AML/CTF supervisor for licensed banks; HM Government of Gibraltar as the monetary authority for Gibraltar pound note issuance under the Currency Notes Act 1934; policy alignment with HM Treasury sanctions and financial restrictions; no separate Gibraltar central bank exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange-control laws, no central bank approval gates, and no restrictions on the repatriation of capital, dividends, or profits for a non-resident Bermuda Exempted Company operating through Gibraltar. Practical limitations arise only from bank-level AML/KYC due diligence, HM Treasury sanctions compliance, and the absence of a domestic interbank FX market, requiring settlement through major London or European correspondent banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Gibraltarian law imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory repayment of export proceeds, and no minimum conversion ratio into Gibraltar pounds. Export-related receipts, including EdTech subscription fees, may be held indefinitely in any convertible currency at a GFSC-licensed bank. However, a licensed bank may request supporting invoices, contracts, and payment evidence for any credit exceeding approximately GBP 100,000 to satisfy its AML/CTF reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multi-Currency Account; Capital Escrow Account available on relationship approval
Operational Account / Foreign-Currency Account; Escrow Account subject to separate commercial approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Moderate. A GFSC-licensed or recognised EEA/UK electronic money institution (EMI) can be used as an auxiliary payment-composition facility for digital settlement with Apple and Google, online card acquirers, and low-value vendor payouts. Legal constraints are decisive: EMIs are not licensed to take deposits, issue commercial letters of credit, open statutory capital escrow accounts, or deliver bilateral FX hedging products. Therefore, the Bermuda Exempted Company must retain at least one full-reserve corporate bank account with a tier-1 GFSC-licensed bank for capital injections, escrow, and FX trade. The offshore EMI may only act as a pass-through collection account, and any funds held in an EMI must remain segregated from the EMI's own balance sheet.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar law does not mandate physical attendance by directors for company account opening, but GFSC AML/CTF rules and each bank's internal policy govern the actual procedure. For a Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident shareholders, a tier-1 bank will generally permit remote onboarding using video-identification and certified electronic documents, provided that the UBO appears for a video interview and the registered agent in Gibraltar provides a formal introduction. Physical presence at the Gibraltar bank's office is typically required only when: (i) the bank classes the structure as high-risk, (ii) the client requests a commercial letter of credit or treasury line, or (iii) the bank cannot verify the certified passport documents electronically. For this EdTech subscription entity, remote opening is realistic with a strong corporate-pack completeness score.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company status with non-resident ownership presenting an 'offshore shell' inference.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Exemption, Register of Members, Register of Directors, Beneficial Ownership Register filed under Gibraltar's beneficial-ownership framework, group organisation chart showing the ultimate parent and economic purpose, certificate of incumbency from the registered agent, and signed declarations from each UBO confirming source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No economic substance or circular management concerns under Gibraltar substance rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance self-assessment report, Gibraltar premises lease or serviced-office agreement, payroll and social-insurance records for employees, reasoned board minutes held in Gibraltar, service contracts with any corporate-service-provider, and a transfer-pricing documentation bundle evidencing that the EdTech IP licensing and management decisions are not merely paper arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital EdTech revenue through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing creating card-not-present and consumer-refund risk flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Apple and Google, periodic platform settlement statements, refund policy documentation, transaction monitoring framework, PCI DSS compliance attestation from the payment processor, and a low-chargeback historical record from the operating jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intercompany capital injections or royalty flows from a Bermuda exempt parent to the Gibraltar operating account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-resolved capital subscription agreement, intercompany licensing or cost-sharing agreement, source-of-funds documentation from the remitting bank, SWIFT MT103 confirmations for prior transfers, audited financial statements of the Bermuda entity, and tax advice confirming that no UK/Gibraltar withholding or tax-evasion offence is engaged.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inward routing is by SWIFT MT103 from the Bermuda parent or investor bank into the Gibraltar tier-1 bank's operational or escrow account. The MT103 must carry a purpose narrative such as 'Capital Injection -- Equity Contribution for EdTech Operations' and should reference: (i) the beneficiary account at the Gibraltar bank using BIC and IBAN-like local account number; (ii) the corporate resolution date authorising the injection; and (iii) the ultimate beneficial owner's source-of-funds details. Verification on receipt follows GFSC AML/CTF controls: the bank will match the remitter against approved KYC records, confirm that the Bermuda entity is not subject to HM Treasury sanctions, and request a board resolution and capital account entry for any inbound amount exceeding a bank-defined threshold, typically GBP 100,000. No cash flows, third-party intermediary transfers, or cryptocurrency-funded injections are acceptable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard operational disbursements, license fees, vendor payments, and profit distributions are executed as SWIFT MT103 messages cleared through London correspondent banks via CHAPS for GBP or through the New York clearing system for USD. For larger infrastructure or content-licensing procurements, the Gibraltar bank may issue an irrevocable at-sight commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600, with the beneficiary bank confirming or advising the LC; settlement is against presentation of commercial invoice, transport or delivery document, inspection certificate, and beneficiary certificate where necessary. EdTech platform payouts from Apple and Google are received first into the operating account via a local clearing or acquirer settlement and then onward-dispatched by MT103 to the Bermuda entity or operating subsidiaries, with each outward transfer supported by contract references and, where relevant, intercompany invoicing. Profit repatriation is permitted in any convertible currency and should be narrated as 'Profit Distribution' with audited financials and board minutes available on demand.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in GBP/USD/EUR with a GFSC-licensed bank or an FCA-regulated counterparty, limited to notional amounts backed by forecast EdTech subscriptions and known trade payables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging or restricted currencies where physical delivery into Gibraltar is not possible, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, and subject to the bank's credit risk approval.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-term intercompany loan exposure arising from the Bermuda parent's capital injection into the Gibraltar operational entity.
Plain-vanilla FX swaps for managing same-week liquidity between subscription revenue, vendor payments, and dividend repatriation, without speculative leverage or unapproved complex option structures.

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% standard Gibraltar corporate income tax rate applicable to the Bermuda Exempted Company's chargeable profits derived through Gibraltar trading activity
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar imposes a 5% preferential corporate rate for licensed qualifying sectors (online gambling, broadcasting, utilities and fuel-related operations); the EdTech language-learning subscription business is outside those sectors and is assessed at 12.5%. Bermuda applies zero per cent income tax to the Exempted Company, but this exemption does not supersede Gibraltar source-state taxation where trading operations, management and control, or a permanent establishment sit in Gibraltar. No tax on capital gains or corporate dividends arises in Gibraltar or Bermuda. Trading losses sustained by the Gibraltar-assessed business may be offset against future profits only to the extent permitted by the Gibraltar Income Tax Act, with the applicable statutory carry-forward limit fixed at 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Corporation Tax Return (statutory Company Return under the Income Tax Act 2010) filed electronically through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Filing portal (Government of Gibraltar online tax services)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be delivered on or before 30 November in the year following the year of assessment in which the accounting period ends; for a December year-end the return is due by 30 November of the following year, with the related self-assessed tax payable by the same date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification block: registered name, Gibraltar income tax reference number, Companies House Gibraltar incorporation number, registered office in Gibraltar, and global ultimate parent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Bermuda Exempted Company must enter its full Bermuda legal name, Bermuda exempted company number, and, if applicable, the Gibraltar branch or place-of-business registration number; a local tax representative should be appointed where the company has no Gibraltar registered office

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment and basis period: start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return, and confirmation that the basis period matches the statutory year of assessment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers with non-calendar-year financial statements must reconcile the Bermuda reporting year with the Gibraltar basis period; where the Bermuda Exempted Company uses a 31 March year-end, the Gibraltar return must follow the Gibraltar assessment year and may require separate apportionment of the trading results

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross trading receipts: total worldwide gross subscription revenue from the interactive language education and automated tutoring software, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing gross billings before platform commissions, and any direct B2B licence fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits attributable to Gibraltar-source trading activity are chargeable if the company is managed and controlled offshore; revenue from contracts concluded by or through the Gibraltar operation and from sales booked through Gibraltar payment accounts must be declared in full; platform commissions should be shown as a deduction, not netted against turnover

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: operating expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for the taxable trade, including content hosting, software development, employee salaries, app-store platform fees, legal and accounting costs, and EMI/banking charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must restrict deductions to expenses attributable to the Gibraltar-source trade; intra-group charges to the Bermuda parent are deductible only where arm's length transfer pricing documentation is maintained; no deduction is allowed for notional management charges without real services and supporting time/cost records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances and reliefs: claims for statutory capital allowances on qualifying plant, machinery, computer hardware and capitalised software development, together with any group relief or loss relief claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bermuda Exempted Companies claiming capital allowances on assets used partly outside Gibraltar must apportion the allowance to the Gibraltar-source trade; software platforms licensed from the Bermuda parent are not eligible for capital allowances unless legal and beneficial ownership has passed to the Gibraltar taxable entity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted chargeable profits and tax computation: total assessable profits after adding back disallowables, deducting allowances, applying the 12.5% headline rate (or 5% for qualifying licensed activities) and setting against the resulting figure any non-refundable foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must ensure that the profit apportionment formula is supported by contemporaneous working papers; the Bermuda zero-rate regime generates no foreign tax credit, so no relief should be claimed for Bermuda 'tax' absent an actual foreign tax suffered; the Gibraltar tax due must be computed in Gibraltar pounds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable, payments on account and repayment claim: balance of Gibraltar corporation tax due after deducting provisional payments, or claim to repayment where credits and withheld amounts exceed the final liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with no Gibraltar permanent establishment staff should still file to evidence the Gibraltar tax position and to obtain the digital tax residency certificate required for EMI banking and treaty relief; any balance of tax must be paid electronically by the statutory deadline

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed statutory penalty of up to £500, escalating daily default surcharges for continued non-compliance, and tax-geared penalties of up to 100% of the tax understated for negligent or deliberate errors; statutory interest accrues on all unpaid corporation tax from the due date until settlement, and deliberate evasion can additionally trigger criminal prosecution and publication of the taxpayer's name as a deliberate defaulter

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Economic Substance (EC) Declaration and annual exempted company return filed through the Bermuda Registrar of Companies online Compliance Portal (Bermuda corporate registry e-services)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 30 June in the year following the end of the Bermuda exempted company's financial year; for a 31 December financial year-end the EC Declaration is due by 30 June of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bermuda exempted company identification: registered name, Bermuda company number, date of incorporation, registered office in Bermuda, and contact details of the Bermuda resident secretary or registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Gibraltar-assessed Bermuda Exempted Company must identify itself accurately as a Bermuda-incorporated foreign-resident entity if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, and must attach the Gibraltar tax residency certificate or assessment evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity election: declaration of whether the company carries on a relevant activity for Bermuda ESR purposes, including intellectual property business, distribution and service business, financing or pure holding company status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An EdTech subscription business licensing software and selling automated tutoring services should declare either intellectual property business or distribution and service business; where the company is tax-resident in Gibraltar, the 'tax resident elsewhere' box must be completed and supported by the Gibraltar assessment or tax residency certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial and substance data: gross income from the EdTech activity, total operating expenditure, number of employees and key management personnel, and the location and nature of core income-generating activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities claiming tax-residency in Gibraltar must evidence where employees, servers, contracts and bank accounts are located; the Bermuda declaration should not show Bermuda substance that is not genuinely operated, because cross-border information exchange will identify inconsistencies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance attestation: signed confirmation by a director or officer that the economic substance test is satisfied or that the company is tax-resident in a qualifying foreign jurisdiction, together with details of any outsourcing arrangements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors of the Bermuda Exempted Company must personally sign the declaration; knowingly false statements expose the director to criminal penalties, and reliance on 'tax resident elsewhere' status is invalid unless the company actually pays corporation tax at a commercial rate in Gibraltar

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Bermuda EC Declaration attracts a fixed penalty of BMD 10,000; serious non-compliance, including failure of the substance test for an intellectual property business, repeated failures for two consecutive periods, or failure to pay penalties, attracts penalties up to BMD 250,000, potential strike-off and deregistration, and mandatory exchange of information with United Kingdom and Gibraltar competent authorities

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar-resident company to any shareholder, whether resident or non-resident, and Bermuda levies no dividend withholding tax on the Bermuda Exempted Company; repatriation of profits by dividend to a Bermuda or United Kingdom beneficial owner is therefore free of source-state dividend withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bermuda has no comprehensive double tax agreement with Gibraltar or the United Kingdom, so no treaty claim is necessary for dividends flowing from the Bermuda Exempted Company to its shareholders. Where the ultimate beneficial owner is United Kingdom-resident, the United Kingdom-Gibraltar double tax agreement (effective 1 January 2020) applies: the beneficial owner must file a claim with HMRC and the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the respective tax authority, complete the relevant administrative relief application, and confirm beneficial ownership before the dividend or interest payment is made; electronic TRC validation and annual treaty entitlement statements may be required to secure relief at source on UK-sourced royalty and interest payments
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Gibraltar statutory withholding tax on cross-border IP royalties and debt interest is 0%; under the United Kingdom-Gibraltar double tax agreement, United Kingdom and Gibraltar source-state withholding on royalties and interest is reduced to 0% for beneficial owners, although the United Kingdom's domestic 20% royalty withholding tax requires a formal treaty claim; Apple IAP and Google Play Billing commissions of up to 30% are commercial platform fees, not royalties, and are not subject to royalty withholding but must be justified under transfer pricing rules

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP/GBP 1,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers the expectation of full OECD-aligned Master File and Local File documentation for the Bermuda Exempted Company and any Gibraltar operating entity; below the threshold a contemporaneous summary transfer pricing analysis, benchmarking note and intercompany agreement register are strongly recommended to withstand Gibraltar, Bermuda and UK audits
